name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Grijalva with large fundraising edge
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Grijalva: a D+13 district, incumbency, and a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage over Butierez, who has almost no cash on hand. Prediction markets price the race at about 99% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D call.
model.watch: A surprise polling error or unusually low turnout in a low-profile special-style race could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adelita Grijalva, the Democratic incumbent in a Tucson-based district that leans Democratic by about thirteen points, is seeking a full term after winning the seat. She has raised over $2.2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Daniel Butierez has raised only about $224,000 with under $12,000 on hand and no meaningful outside support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money, both of which favor Democrats decisively. Prediction markets price Grijalva's chances at roughly 99%, and the expected margin is in the low twenties, making this a Safe Democratic seat.
